newsitem.title: USA: Mycogen Seeds to send corn seed to N Korea.
newsitem.headline: Mycogen Seeds to send corn seed to N Korea.

text.p: A U.S. firm has donated 35 tons of hybrid corn seed for shipment to hunger-stricken North Korea, the relief agency World Vision said Thursday.
The grain, which is expected to yield 7,000 to 14,000 tons of corn will come from Mycogen Seeds in St. Paul, Minn., the relief agency said.
Shipment, distribution and planting of the corn seed will be monitored by a team of relief workers and an agronomist provided by World Vision, a spokeswoman said.
The seeds will be shipped from Seattle to Inchon, South Korea on April 11 and will be used to replenish food supplies.
The corn seeds being shipped to North Korea are no longer sold in the U.S., but a spokesperson for Mycogen said the seeds were "very viable for planting."

Earlier this week, Cargill Inc announced a barter deal with North Korea. Cargill did not disclose the amount of wheat involved in the deal, but traders in Seoul said Cargill would ship 20,000 tonnes of wheat to North Korea in exchange for 4,000 tonnes of zinc.
